transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is... I'm just having a lot of trouble organizing things lately. 

There are just too many moving parts anymore. Um... patent notes, team decisions at work... and then some other things, like workshop prep and gallery deadlines. I just can't seem to keep it all straight. I usually just end up starting whatever is loudest... instead of what actually matters. 

So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
Did you have this same kind of trouble with organizing and keeping track of things when you were a child?

Yeah... I suppose so. Um, looking back, it was there in grade school, too. Teachers usually wrote that I was bright, but... that I daydreamed a lot. 

I would forget to turn in assignments I had actually finished, or... I'd just lose my homework folders. So, yeah. That was all long before I was a teenager.
Do these attention and organization problems cause significant problems in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

Um... I suppose. I mean, it's mostly just what I already mentioned... with work and my own projects. I haven't really... I don't know. I guess it's just a general issue. I haven't really thought about it much beyond that.
Do these attention and organization problems also cause trouble for you at home?

Um... I guess so. I mean, my house is a bit cluttered, but... I don't know if it's really a problem. It's just how I live. I mostly just focus on work and my projects, so... the house just kind of is what it is.
At home, have these attention and organization problems caused real problems for you?
I don't think so. I mean... not really. Like I said, it's just a bit messy. I don't really have people over anyway, so... it doesn't bother anyone. It's just my space.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn't an immediate problem to solve?
Um... no, I don't think so. I'm not really much of a worrier. I just... I don't know, if something comes up I deal with it, but... otherwise, no. Not really.
Have these attention and organization problems caused difficulties in your relationships with other people?
Uh... no, not really. I mostly just keep to myself, so... I haven't really noticed any issues there.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Uh... no. I wouldn't say that. I feel fine, mostly. Just... normal, I guess.
Have these attention and organization problems caused real problems for you at work?

Yeah... I suppose it has. Um... it's kind of starting to affect my reputation there. I, uh... I missed a checkpoint for a patent filing recently. And then we had this architecture review that... well, it was pretty rough. Now some of the people I work with are... they're sort of questioning if I can actually lead the larger project. So... yeah. It's an issue.
Outside of work, have these attention and organization problems caused a serious problem in any part of your life?

Um... no. Not really. Like I said earlier, I mostly just keep to myself outside of work. My life is pretty quiet. I don't really do much that takes a lot of organization, I guess. So... no, nothing serious.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Um... sometimes, I guess. Like, if I'm on one of those really long design calls... I start feeling this, um, pressure building up in my body. Like I just need to get up. So I end up pacing around my office a lot. Or I just keep shifting from chair to chair... even when I'm trying to look focused.
Have these attention and organization problems ever caused a serious problem for you in school?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, school was fine. I got through my degree without any major issues. It wasn't really a problem back then.
When you were in grade school, did your inattention or disorganization ever get you into real trouble at school?

I mean... not real trouble, I guess. But... looking back, it was definitely there in grade school. My teachers would always write that I was bright, but... that I daydreamed too much. And, um... I used to lose my homework folders a lot. Or I'd actually finish an assignment and just... forget to turn it in. So... yeah. That was happening long before I was a teenager.
When you’ve been away from work for a while, do these attention and organization problems get a lot better?
Um... I haven't really noticed. I don't think they get better, no. It's... pretty much the same even if I take time off.
Have these attention and organization problems ever caused a serious problem in managing everyday tasks outside of work?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I guess I manage okay at home. It's... it's fine.
Did these problems start mainly after your work responsibilities became more demanding?
Um... no. I mean, like I said... it was already happening back in grade school. So... no, it didn't just start with work.
Do you often make careless mistakes because your attention drifts?

Um... yeah, I suppose. At work, doing code reviews... I'll miss something pretty small. Like a reversed condition, or a version number in a dependency file. It's... kind of embarrassing. Later I can see it was right in front of me, but I just... skimmed past it.
Have these attention problems put your job at risk?

I mean... I don't know if I'm about to be fired. But... it's definitely damaging my reputation there. I, um... I missed a checkpoint on a patent filing recently. And... there was an architecture review that went pretty badly. I think some of the collaborators are starting to question if I can actually lead the larger project. So... yeah. It's becoming a problem.
Have these attention problems ever caused you to miss paying a bill on time?
Um... no. Not really. My wife handles most of the finances, so... I don't really deal with the bills.
